docs.title: ADR-062: Newton, a verifiable math/physics engine
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-11 · Status: Accepted (awaiting laptop install)
Ahmad asked for a "Newton brain": a mathematician/physicist agent in Claude and on the site that
computes exact answers for the whole project (car arrival, ship-to-island arrival, more accurate Earth map).
Local LLMs (qwen2.5:3b) and even frontier models are unreliable at arithmetic; numbers must come from code.
- New `newton/` Python package: Vincenty geodesy (WGS84), SymPy exact maths (sandboxed parser: no
  attribute access, no builtins, char allow-list), constant-acceleration kinematics, ship ETA
  (AIS SOG + geodesic legs + optional Open-Meteo surface current vector triangle), road ETA (OSRM/OSM).
- Two front doors over the same functions: MCP stdio server `omega-newton` (read-only, compute only)
  and a loopback HTTP API + Arabic dark page on 127.0.0.1:8095.
- Every result carries inputs, formula, assumptions, evidence URLs and a ±1 kn sensitivity for ships.
- Free/keyless only. Port 8095 chosen to avoid 8088 (relay), 8089/8090 (Cortex), 8890 (SearXNG).
- "Econo-physics" Navier-Stokes market engine (PINNs + Lean agents + Kubernetes): markets do not obey a
  known conservation law, so a PINN has no true physics to enforce; Lean can prove a statement, not a
  forecast. Kubernetes is overkill for one laptop. If ever built: experimental signal on paper trading,
  backtested, CCXT read-only, never real orders.
- Context: OpenAI announced a Lean-verified Navier-Stokes blow-up proof on 2026-09-08; not yet
  independently reviewed, Clay has not awarded, and credit is disputed (Buckmaster/Alpöge). It is pure
  maths about idealised fluids and gives no trading edge.
- Oracle/Claude can answer "when does X arrive" with checkable numbers.
- Next (needs approval): Earth screen click-a-ship -> "ETA to..." using Newton; self-hosted OSRM for GCC.

docs.title: ADR-063: Phone access over Tailscale (tailnet only)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-15 · Status: Accepted (verified on the phone 2026-10-15)
Ahmad wants to open the OMEGA site from his phone away from home (4G), not only on home Wi-Fi.
The existing Caddy setup (ops/caddy) only serves the LAN on https://<lan-ip>:8443 with a local CA that
the phone must trust. Opening a port on the router or exposing the site publicly is not acceptable.
- Tailscale 1.104.1 on the laptop, signed in with Ahmad's Google account; the phone joins the same tailnet.
- `tailscale serve` publishes https://<laptop>.<tailnet>.ts.net -> http://127.0.0.1:3100,
  tailnet only. Tailscale issues a real Let's Encrypt certificate for the ts.net name, so the phone
  needs no custom CA.
- Funnel stays OFF: nobody outside the tailnet can reach the site.
- The web app keeps binding to 127.0.0.1 only; Caddy keeps serving the LAN path unchanged. Tailscale
  does not go through Caddy, so a Caddy outage does not break remote access (and vice versa).
- No repo code changes; Serve config lives in the Tailscale client, not in git.
- `tailscale serve status`: `https://<laptop>.<tailnet>.ts.net (tailnet only) |-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:3100`
- From the laptop: `/ar` -> 200, `ssl_verify_result=0`, `<title>القيادة</title>`, `dir="rtl"`.
- Caddy (ops/caddy/start-https.ps1): `https://localhost:8443/ar` -> 200.
- iPhone joined the tailnet; Ahmad opened the URL on it and the page loaded.
Phoenix exited with code 1 on every run while Docker/Postgres was down, so it did not restart the web app or Caddy
after a reboot. ADR-064 fixes it.
- Port forwarding on the router: exposes the laptop to the internet.
- Tailscale Funnel: public URL; not needed for a single user.
- Cloudflare Tunnel: next step in the plan (with TOTP), decided separately.

docs.title: docs/adr/ADR-064-autostart-after-reboot.md
docs.text:
﻿# ADR-064: OMEGA comes back by itself after a reboot (Windows)
Date: 2026-10-15 · Status: Accepted (installed 2026-10-15 with Ahmad's OK)
Ahmad asked for Docker and the OMEGA services to restart automatically after the laptop reboots, phrased as a
systemd unit. The laptop runs Windows 11, so systemd does not exist here; the equivalents are Docker Desktop's
own sign-in autostart, compose restart policies and Task Scheduler.
Found on 2026-10-15:
- "OMEGA Phoenix" (ADR-020) failed every 5 minutes (Last Result 1). `from_env()` opened the Postgres event log
  on :5435 before healing anything; with Docker down after a reboot that raised `InterfaceError`, so the
  `memory_restart` step that starts Docker was never reached.
- Docker Desktop had `AutoStart: false` and its startup entry was disabled, so the engine never came up.
- Every long-running service in docker-compose.yml already has `restart: unless-stopped` (the `x-hardening`
  anchor). One-shots (`db-migrate`, `n8n-init`, `ollama-pull`) and the opt-in `ollama` keep `restart: "no"` on
  purpose (7 GB laptop).
- Phoenix falls back to the SQLite event log when Postgres cannot be reached, so the heal pass runs and starts
  Docker + the `memory` container; the next pass logs to Postgres again.
- `ops/autostart/omega-boot.ps1`: start Docker Desktop if the engine is not answering (wait up to 4 min),
  `docker compose --profile director up -d memory` (every other container that was running returns through its own
  `restart: unless-stopped`; a full `up -d` would also create n8n, relay, agents and quant, ~1.1 GB that never ran
  here, and `compose start` fails on quant's missing relay dependency), then the web app on 127.0.0.1:3100 via secure-run (ADR-042) if
  nothing listens there. It never stops anything. Log: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OMEGA\boot.log`.
- `ops/autostart/install-autostart.ps1` (run once by Ahmad): turns on Docker Desktop's "start when you sign in",
  re-enables its startup entry, and registers the per-user task "OME

docs.title: ADR-077: Agent system design: brains, nervous system and long-term memory (design only)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (design document, nothing built)
Ahmad asked (2026-10-16) for a deep, open-source-first design of the agents: specialised agents with their own
roles, tools and computers; a shared nervous system; long-term memory; a brain that plans, researches, analyses and
acts; plus the wallet, an RR unit and a "Swiss banking" style system. Limits from the project: no real money, custody,
exchange keys or orders; agents only add proposals to the approval queue and a human approves each one (ADR-073,
ADR-076); every agent discloses it is an AI (`docs/AGENT-DISCLOSURE.md` on the paper-trading branch).
- Design lives in `docs/agents/ARCHITECTURE-AGENTS.md` (Arabic summary first, technical detail after).
- Two loops: a no-LLM reflex layer on the existing stream bus, and a LangGraph deliberation loop with Postgres
  checkpoints and hard budgets.
- Nervous system inside the existing Postgres: hash-chained append-only event log, pgmq queues per agent, a registry
  of A2A-style Agent Cards, and an MCP tool gateway that enforces per-agent allow-lists from data, not prompts.
- Memory in the existing pgvector service: working, episodic, semantic (bitemporal), procedural and a calibration
  ledger that scores every forecast; a nightly consolidation ("sleep") run.
- Ten agents, including the existing four; only فهد has `proposals.add`, and no agent has any approve or fill tool.
- Wallet, RR unit and Vault are paper and read-only; the Vault is stated not to be a bank, with a licence review
  required before any non-paper use.
- Proposes swapping `redis:7.4` (RSALv2/SSPL) for Valkey (BSD-3) in phase 1.
- Research table: 59 projects checked from their official repositories for licence and last commit on 2026-10-16.
- No code changes in this commit. Seven phases (second brain is phase 3, ADR-078), each gated on Ahmad's approval, one commit and one ADR each.
- Phase 5 (market agents) depends on the paper-trading MVP (ADR-073 to ADR-076) being merged.
- Undo: de

docs.title: ADR-078: Second brain: a personal knowledge graph the agents build, with an interactive graph view (design only)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (design document, nothing built)
Ahmad (2026-10-16 11:43Z) asked to add a "second brain" to the agent design: for someone who overthinks, the AI should
sort the crowd of ideas, link them, and become a mind that thinks with him, shown as an interactive graph like an
Obsidian-style graph view (screenshot), with search and filters on nodes and links.
- New section 12 in `docs/agents/ARCHITECTURE-AGENTS.md`.
- Pipeline: capture (no questions asked) → raw note kept verbatim → atomise → enrich (local embedding, entities,
  type) → suggested edges with confidence and a reason → Leiden clusters named in Arabic → graph.
- Machine edges stay "suggested" (dashed) until Ahmad accepts; his accepts and rejects tune the linker.
- Overthinking features: brain dump, loop detector, worry → question, daily collision, contradiction alarm, decision
  journal tied to the calibration ledger, "think with me" chat that answers from his graph and cites nodes.
- Graph view: sigma.js + graphology (2D, WebGL), 3d-force-graph (3D constellation mode); search by text and meaning,
  filters, time slider, focus, path, evidence panel.
- Storage: `brain.raw / nodes / edges` in the existing pgvector Postgres; Apache AGE only if graph queries grow.
- Private by default: local model only, per-note opt-in for cloud, separate from agent memory, never a proposal source;
  nightly Markdown export with `[[wikilinks]]` (Foam format) so his notes are never locked in.
- Research: 32 more projects checked from their official repositories (licence, last commit, 2026-10-16). Avoided:
  SSPL, BSL, custom-restricted, GPL where an MIT equivalent exists, archived or abandoned projects.
- Phase 3 in the plan, right after memory (Ahmad's choice, 2026-10-16). No new server and no paid key.
- Undo: delete section 12 and this ADR.

docs.title: ADR-079: Agents phase 1: the nervous system (event log, registry, tool gateway, queues) and Valkey
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Ahmad approved phase 1 of the agent design (ADR-077) on 2026-10-16 ("موافق اكمله"). Phase 1 needs no LLM and no
keys: it builds the wiring every later agent uses.
- `db/init/05-nerve.sh` adds schema `nerve` to the existing Timescale/Postgres (no new server):
  - `nerve.events`: append-only (update, delete and truncate refused by triggers) and hash-chained: each row stores
    `sha256(previous hash | row)`, with the id taken under one advisory lock so id order is chain order.
    `nerve.verify_chain(n)` recomputes the last n rows (or all) and names the first broken row.
  - `nerve.agents`: the ten Agent Cards from ADR-077. A row without the Arabic and English AI disclosure is refused
    (ADR-076). Toolbelts may only hold registered tools; a sole-holder tool (proposals.add → فهد, memory.write → أمين,
    agents.pause → حارس, vault.reconcile → خازن) cannot be given to anyone else.
  - `nerve.tools`: a constraint refuses any tool named approve, fill, order, withdraw, transfer, sign, execute, trade,
    wallet_key or custody, so a money-moving tool cannot even be registered (ADR-073).
  - `nerve.tool_call()`: the gateway. Refuses unknown tools, tools outside the toolbelt, paused agents, and tainted
    input driving a write tool; every allow and refusal is an event.
  - `nerve.send / read / ack / expire`: one queue per agent with a visibility timeout (at-least-once), `SKIP LOCKED`,
    `pg_notify('nerve_<agent>')` to wake workers, and an archive with the outcome. A message is never more trusted
    than its sender. Same semantics as pgmq without installing an extension in the Timescale image.
  - `nerve.pause_agent` (حارس or the owner) and `nerve.resume_agent` (owner only).
  - Role `nerve_agent`: execute on the agent functions only; no table access; cannot resume, cannot write or send
    as the owner or system, cannot claim owner/system trust.
  - `api.nerve_agents`, `api.nerve_events`, `api.nerve_chain` for t

docs.title: ADR-080: Agents phase 2: long-term memory (episodes, bitemporal facts, skills, calibration) and أمين
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Ahmad started phase 2 on 2026-10-16 (decision card "ابدأ المرحلة 2"). Design: ADR-077 section 6. Phase 1 (ADR-079)
gave the event log, the registry and the tool gateway this builds on.
- `db/init/06-memory.sh` adds schema `mem` to the same Postgres (no new server):
  - `mem.episodes`: what happened. Any agent logs through `mem.log_episode`; archived after 30 days, still searchable.
  - `mem.facts`: bitemporal beliefs (`valid_from/valid_to` = world time, `recorded_at/superseded_at` = when we learned
    and dropped it). One current row per subject+predicate. The same belief from a new source confirms it (more
    sources, no duplicate); a different one supersedes the old row, which is kept. Overturning a belief held with
    confidence ≥ 0.8 writes `memory.contradiction` for بدر. Content is never edited and rows are never deleted,
    except by `mem.forget_user` (owner only).
  - Write gate: facts only via `mem.assert_fact`, which goes through the nerve gateway (`memory.write`, sole holder
    أمين); evidence is required (http(s) links or event ids); facts from tainted sources start `unverified` until a
    second independent source; key-shaped strings (API keys, tokens, private keys, JWTs) are refused, nothing is
    stored, and a `guard.secret_refused` event (without the secret) is logged.
  - `mem.skills`: procedures with use/success counts; a skill is a draft until بدر (or the owner) reviews it; the
    nightly sleep retires skills that fail more than half the time after 5 uses.
  - `mem.forecasts` + `mem.calibration`: the calibration ledger. Each resolved forecast gets a Brier score; an agent
    can never grade its own forecast; resolving needs evidence. `skill_vs_coin` > 0 means better than always 50%.
  - `mem.search`: hybrid recall over current facts (or the facts believed at a past time, `p_as_of`) and episodes:
    full-text (Arabic and English, `simple` config, OR of the words) + cosine similarity

docs.title: ADR-081: Agents phase 3: the second brain (capture, atoms, links, themes, rescue, map, Markdown export)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Ahmad approved phase 3 on 2026-10-16 ("ابدأ المرحلة 3"). Design: ADR-078 and `docs/agents/ARCHITECTURE-AGENTS.md`
section 12. Phases 1 and 2 (ADR-079, ADR-080) give the event log, the tool gateway and the memory keeper this builds on.
The second brain is Ahmad's own private graph of thoughts. It is separate from the agents' memory and can never
become a trading proposal.
- **Schema `brain`** in the same Postgres (`db/init/07-brain.sh`, no new server):
  - `brain.raw`: every capture, verbatim. Append-only; only the owner's `brain.forget_user` (admin login) can erase it.
  - `brain.nodes`: atoms, one idea, question, task, fact, worry, decision, quote or source each, pointing at their raw note.
    Text and type never change; cluster and embedding may be recomputed.
  - `brain.edges`: links with `origin` (human | machine), `confidence`, a one-line `why` and `state`
    (suggested | accepted | rejected). Machine links start `suggested`; the owner's taps decide, and a decision is final.
    A rejected link is never suggested again (the unique key keeps it).
  - `brain.clusters`, `brain.settings`: themes, and the thresholds the owner's taps tune (accept lowers the similarity
    threshold, reject raises it).
- **Gated functions only.** No agent reads or writes a `brain` table. Three new tools in the gateway:
  `brain.read` (hakeem, ameen), `brain.write` and `brain.link` (sole holder ameen). Every function refuses an agent
  that acts under another name (`brain.guard_session`), and refuses a secret before storage (`mem.looks_secret`).
- **Events carry ids and counts, never words.** The event log is published read-only by the relay, so the brain writes
  `brain.captured`, `brain.atom`, `brain.suggested`, `brain.decided`, `brain.clustered` with ids only. The event kind
  constraint gained the `brain` family.

docs.title: ADR-082: Agents phase 4: the brain loop (plan, research, critique, answer, checkpoints, budgets)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Ahmad approved phase 4 on 2026-10-16 ("المرحلة 4 ثم 6"). Design: ADR-077 section 4. Phases 1 to 3 (ADR-079 to
ADR-081) give the event log, the gateway, the memory keeper and the second brain this builds on.
- **Schema `loop`** (`db/init/08-loop.sh`):
  - `loop.runs`: one row per run. The goal lives here and never in the event log. Budgets (`max_steps`, `max_tokens`)
    and counters are enforced by the database.
  - `loop.checkpoints`: one row per node, append-only. A run resumes from its last checkpoint after a restart
    (`loop.resume`).
  - A step past a budget stops the run as `incomplete`; the database records it, and the last checkpoint keeps what the
    run had. A secret in a checkpoint fails the run and nothing is stored.
- **Who runs it.** Only عبدالله (the planner) holds `loop.run` (sole holder). Maha and Badr have no database tool in
  this phase: their steps are functions the planner's runner calls (search and critique). The design had them as
  separate agents with separate prompts; the separation of prompts and roles is kept in code, and the
  database-level separation (who may write a checkpoint) is kept by the sole-holder rule.
- **Nodes:** perceive, recall (`mem.search`, the agents' memory, not the second brain), plan, research (SearXNG,
  keyless, every result tainted), analyse, critique (بدر's rules), propose (an answer only), learn (an episode with the
  outcome and the source count, never the question).
- **Critic (`services/loop/critic.py`):** no sources → gap; fewer than two independent domains → gap; an answer that
  cites no source → gap. Gaps send the plan back at most `max_rounds` times (default 2), then the run stops
  `incomplete` with the gaps listed.
- **Models (`services/loop/models.py`):** extractive by default: plan with the goal and the recall, answer only with
  source lines and their links. The Cortex path (free routes through the gateway) runs only when `CORTEX_URL` an

docs.title: ADR-083: Agents phase 5: the market agents and the paper gate (two keys and an owner)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Phase 5 of ADR-077 section 3 and 8. Phases 1 to 4 (ADR-079 to ADR-082) give the event log, the gateway, memory,
the second brain and the loop. The coordinator asked for phases 4 to 7 on the draft branch with no execution path.
The paper-trading MVP lives on `feat/paper-trading-mvp` and is not merged here, so this phase links to no account.
- **Schema `prop`** (`db/init/09-market.sh`), one table: `prop.proposals`. Long setups only (stop < entry < target),
  size held between 50 and 200 USDT in paper units, the reward-to-risk computed in SQL.
- **Two keys and an owner.**
  - فهد (`proposals.add`, sole holder) packs an idea with its evidence (a link or an event id). Refused without evidence.
  - راشد (`risk.check`, sole holder after this change) passes a proposal only at a reward-to-risk of 2 or more.
    A thin setup gets `risk_fail` with the reason; it is kept, not deleted.
  - The owner decides (`prop.decide`). No agent holds the grant, and the function refuses agent callers. It accepts
    only a checked proposal (`risk_pass`).
- **Immutable proposals.** A trigger refuses any change to the numbers, refuses deletes, and makes a decided proposal
  final. A new idea is a new row.
- **No execution path.** The `prop` schema holds one table and no function whose name suggests an order, a fill, a
  transfer or a sale. The test checks that. `approved` means approved on paper; nothing reads it to act.
- **Public queue.** `api.prop_queue` (titles, numbers, status, the risk reason; no rationale, no evidence) for the
  owner's page. `web_anon` never reads the table.
- **Audit.** Events carry ids and numbers (`proposal.created`, `proposal.checked`, `human.decided`), never a title
  or a rationale. A key pasted into a proposal is refused and nothing is stored.
- `risk.check` is now a sole-holder tool (rashid) and a write. The seed had no holder, so any agent could have been
  granted the check. The sole-holder rule caugh

docs.title: ADR-084: Agents phase 6: the offices, the guide and the disclosure on every page
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Phase 6 of ADR-077. Ahmad needs to see who the agents are, what each may use and what each may not, and whether
one is paused, in plain Arabic. Every agent says it is an AI (ADR-076), and every page should say so too.
- **`/offices`** (`dashboard/offices/index.html`): one card per agent from `api.nerve_agents` (web_anon view): Arabic
  and English name, role, status (a paused agent shows in red with who paused it and why), tools, what it cannot do,
  its container, the queue depth, last activity and its own disclosure line. No CDN, no fonts, text set with
  `textContent` (no HTML from the database). `?demo` shows a fixture for review without the database.
- **`/offices/guide`** (`dashboard/offices/guide.html`): Noura's glossary in Arabic. It explains the agents, and the
  terms a beginner meets: owner, proposal, two keys, RR, paper, Vault, hash chain, budget, checkpoint, tainted input,
  evidence, pause, disclosure. It says what each term does not mean (for example, "paper" is not money).
- **Disclosure banner** on `/offices`, `/offices/guide` and `/mind`. It states in Arabic and English that the user is
  talking to AI agents, that none is a bank, and that none acts for the user. The loop has no page of its own; its
  answers appear on the second brain page, which carries the banner.
- **Relay**: the static page map (`PAGE_FILES`, renamed from `MIND_FILES`) serves the offices pages under the same
  strict CSP as the map (no inline style from outside, `connect-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`). The CSP now
  follows the content type (any HTML page), not the path.
- The offices page reads one view and does no writes. Pausing an agent stays with the owner's tools (ADR-079); the page
  shows the pause, it does not offer a button.
- Last-activity time is shown as a local date string; the view gives the raw time.
- Checked in a headless browser at a phone width (390 px): 3 cards with 1 paused, the guide rend

docs.title: ADR-085: Agents phase 7: the paper Vault (double entry, paper only, not a bank)
headings: Not in this phase (needs a licence review first)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Proposed (draft PR, not merged)
Phase 7 of ADR-077 section 8. Ahmad asked for a professional banking-style ledger. This phase builds the paper
version only, which the design allows: "paper only, with 'not a bank' wording, licence review first". The licence
review for anything beyond paper is open (launch-drafts/LAWYER-QUESTIONS.md) and is not started here.
- **Schema `vault`** (`db/init/10-vault.sh`): a chart of four accounts (paper cash, owner paper capital, paper gains,
  paper fees), a journal, lines (one side per line), reconciliations.
- **Paper only, by construction.** Each account must be `mode = 'paper'` and `currency = 'USDT'` (CHECK). There is no
  bank, custody or exchange table, and no function that moves, pays, withdraws, converts or deposits (the test checks
  the names).
- **Double entry.** `vault.post` refuses an unbalanced entry before writing. A deferred constraint trigger on the
  lines checks the same thing at commit as a backstop for any direct insert. A line has one side only.
- **Append-only.** Journal, lines, accounts and reconciliations refuse UPDATE and DELETE. A mistake is a reversing
  entry.
- **Who does what.** Only the owner posts (`vault.post` has no agent grant). خازن (khazen) holds `vault.reconcile`
  through the gateway (sole holder, already in the seed). Reconcile checks that every journal balances and that the
  paper books satisfy assets = liabilities + equity + income − expenses, stores the result, and logs an event with
  counts only.
- **Public statement.** `api.vault_balances` and `api.vault_statement` (web_anon) show each row labelled
  "ورقي فقط. ليس حساباً بنكياً ولا يحفظ أموالاً. Paper only: not a bank account, holds no funds."
- **Events** carry ids and counts, never a memo. The family `vault` joins the event regex.
- The design had khazen post entries for fills. There are no fills yet (the paper-trading MVP is not merged), so
  posting stays with the owner until that link exists.
- Statement

docs.title: ADR-086: One-brain page (/brain): a local chat that answers from the owner's notes
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-16 · Status: Accepted (merged in PR #17, commit 05b0c83)
Ahmad asked for a one-brain assistant (Claude/ChatGPT-style, free, local-first) and to add it to the site. The design
(`docs/agents/ONE-BRAIN-DESIGN.md`) recommends a thin shell we own, local model first, with no external provider by
default. The licence checks for the candidate bases are incomplete, so this step builds nothing from them.
- **`/brain`** (`dashboard/brain/index.html`): a question box. It posts to the existing second-brain endpoint
  (`/mind/api/think`, ADR-081), which answers only from the owner's own atoms, cites them, and suggests a next question.
  Each citation links to its evidence (`/mind/api/evidence/<n>`).
- **Disclosure** on the page (Arabic and English), as on `/mind` and `/offices`.
- **No provider switch yet.** Nothing leaves the laptop. The free provider path from the Oracle design is a later step,
  behind a per-provider switch set by the owner.
- **Relay**: the page is a static route in the page map (`/brain`), under the same strict HTML CSP as the other pages.
  The question goes to `/mind/api/think`, which the relay already rate-limits.
- Checked in a headless browser at 390 px with the demo fixture: the answer and citation render, no horizontal scroll,
  no console errors. The live think call needs the mind service running (laptop).
- Answers are extractive for now (the phase 3 choice): no generated text, so nothing can invent a fact.

docs.title: ADR-087: Apple HIG design system for site-landing and Ops Room v2
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-18 · Status: Accepted (approved by Ahmad 2026-10-18)
The HIG audit (`audits/HIG-AUDIT-site-landing-ops-room.md`) found sRGB-only colors, no light theme, subtext failing APCA,
fixed px type down to 10px, `100vh`, non-concentric radii and unused glass blur. Ahmad approved the report and three decisions:
white theme first with dark as a toggle, concentric symmetric radii, Cairo plus monospace tabular numbers.
- One OKLCH token set shared by both pages, P3 chroma under `@media (color-gamut: p3)` at the same lightness.
- `--content-tertiary` = oklch(54% 0.039 268) light, oklch(78% 0.039 268) dark. 56.9% from the audit fails on the light
  grey surface (4.40:1), so the gate lowered it. `audits/verify-contrast.mjs` checks every pair (WCAG >= 4.5, APCA Lc >= 60).
- `--ease-apple-fluid` (lowercase) plus a damped spring sampled into `linear()`; only transform and opacity animate.
- Ops Room v2: Canvas 2D globe (no library, so double-click still works), real Binance candles, two-method VaR check,

docs.title: ADR-094: Local server short addresses, same-origin proxy and the file:// hint
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-20 · Status: Accepted (Ahmad's Phase 8 directive in the project thread, 2026-10-20)
ADR-093 made `scripts/omega-data-proxy.mjs` serve the pages, but the addresses were long (`/omega-ops-room-v1/omega-ops-room.html`), both pages hard-coded `http://127.0.0.1:8796` for data, and a copy opened by double-click from disk gave no hint that the server exists. Ahmad asked for one server on port 8796 for all three pages, reachable from the laptop and from the iPhone, with a redirect when a page is opened from `file://`.
1. **Short addresses.** `/omega-ops-room.html`, `/the-chain.html`, `/index.html` and `/en.html` answer 302 to the folder copies and keep the query string. The pages stay inside their folders, so relative links, the manifest and (later) the service worker keep one scope per folder.
2. **Bind address.** Still `127.0.0.1` by default (AGENTS.md §4). `--lan` or `OMEGA_BIND=lan` is an explicit opt-in that listens on `0.0.0.0` and prints the home-network addresses with a warning that anyone on that Wi-Fi can open the pages and the read-only data routes. The proxy stays GET-only with the same upstream allowlist, so `--lan` adds no write path.
3. **Same origin.** A page the proxy served itself (same `Host`, over http or https, for example the iPhone over `--lan` or Tailscale Serve) is allowed as same-origin. Other origins still get 403. Both pages now look for the proxy at `location.origin` first, then at `http://127.0.0.1:8796`, and use whichever answers `/health` with `{"ok":true}`. THE CHAIN adds `'self'` to `connect-src`.
4. **file:// hint.** A page opened from disk shows a status line with a link to the same page on `127.0.0.1:8796` (query and hash kept). If the proxy answers and this disk copy holds no paper wallet, receipts or notes, the page moves itself with `location.replace`. If the copy holds data it stays put and says to export a capsule (Ops Room) or the notes (THE CHAIN) first, because `file://` and `http://127.0.0.1` have separate storage.

docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-20 · Status: Accepted (Ahmad's Phase 8 directive, 2026-10-20)
Ahmad asked that live prices never get the laptop's IP blocked and that SEC EDGAR, OpenSky and GDELT stop returning HTTP 429 or 403. The spot desk already read `data-api.binance.vision` (Binance's public market-data host). Futures data (premium, funding, open interest, long/short and taker ratios) went straight to `fapi.binance.com` from every open tab, the proxy kept only a disk cache, and an upstream 429 was retried on the next page poll.
**Proxy (`scripts/omega-data-proxy.mjs`)**
1. A memory cache (200 entries, oldest out first) sits in front of the existing disk cache. Each route keeps its TTL: SEC tickers 24 h, SEC facts 12 h, OpenSky, GDACS and GDELT 15 min, NGA 30 min, AIS 5 min, Binance spot 30 s, futures 60 s, CoinGecko 2 min.
2. Requests for the same URL while one is in flight share that one upstream call.
3. Each host keeps a minimum gap between calls: SEC 200 ms (10 per second is SEC's published limit), GDELT 5 s (GDELT's guidance), OpenSky 10 s (its anonymous refresh), 250 ms elsewhere.
4. An upstream 429, 418 or 403 pauses that host for its `Retry-After`, with 60 s as the floor (300 s after a 418, which is Binance's IP-ban warning) and 15 min as the ceiling. While paused the proxy serves the stale copy, or answers 503 with `Retry-After` when it has none.
5. `X-Omega-Cache: HIT | MISS | STALE` on every data answer, exposed to local pages through CORS.
6. New route `/market/fapi/<premium|funding|oi|top|global|taker>/<SYMBOL>`, fixed URL templates only, `fapi.binance.com` added to `ALLOWED_UPSTREAM`. The `--check` table adds Binance futures.
7. SEC still requires `OMEGA_SEC_UA`; ADR-094 lets it come from `~/.omega/sec-ua.txt` so the contact stays off git.
**Ops Room desk**
1. The desk's `getJson` pauses a host after 429 or 418, honouring `Retry-After` when the browser can read it (60 s, 300 s after 418, at most 15 min), and waits for the next minute when `x-mbx-used-weight-1m` is

docs.title: ADR-096: Micro-unit money, pure-JS SHA-256 fallback, worker clock and Merkle checkpoints
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-20 · Status: Accepted (Ahmad's Phase 8 directive, 2026-10-20)
Ahmad asked for four hardening items on the paper desk:
- micro-unit rounding (`Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6`) and canonical JSON before SHA-256;
- a pure JavaScript SHA-256 for the iPhone over Wi-Fi;
- a desk timer that does not freeze when the window is minimised;
- automatic compression of old receipts so `localStorage` never fills.
Canonical JSON (keys sorted, numbers to 8 decimals, `hash` left out) was already in place since ADR-091.
1. **Micro-units.** The wallet's USDT fields (`cash`, `base`, `active`, `safe`, `split`, `swept`, `target`, `dayStart`) are rounded to 1e-6 on every save. The receipt `amount` and the before/after snapshots are rounded the same way. BTC quantities keep full precision. The canonical form keeps its 8 decimals: rounding a micro-unit value to 8 decimals changes nothing, so every chain issued before this change still verifies in both verifiers.
2. **Pure SHA-256.**
   - Plain `http://` on the home network is not a secure context, so `crypto.subtle` is undefined there. The Ops Room ledger and the NABD verifier (`site-landing/desk-sim.js`) now carry a FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 in plain JavaScript and use it only when WebCrypto is missing. The Ops Room says "(built-in SHA-256)" after a check.
   - Encryption is not re-implemented. The vault and the capsule keep WebCrypto AES-GCM-256 and PBKDF2, and say to use 127.0.0.1, `file://` or Tailscale HTTPS. A hand-written AES-GCM would be new, unaudited cryptography guarding the only copy of the paper desk.
3. **Worker clock.**
   - Browsers run main-thread timers in a hidden tab at most once a minute, so stops and targets on an open paper position could wait that long. The desk loops now get their ticks from a Blob Web Worker built from a named function (`tickWorker.toString()`, no string code). CSP adds `worker-src 'self' blob:`.
   - While hidden, the 5 s market loop keeps running only when the auto paper engine is on or a paper

docs.text:

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted (Ahmad's Phase 11 directive, 2026-10-22)
The desk polls Binance REST every 5 s. Ahmad asked for:
- the public streams `depth20@100ms` and `aggTrade` from `wss://data-stream.binance.vision`;
- a REST fallback;
- a deterministic simulation when offline.
The trading desk is paper only (ADR-091, ADR-092). No code may sign or send an order.
- **Stream**
  - One combined stream per selected symbol: `wss://data-stream.binance.vision/stream?streams=<sym>@depth20@100ms/<sym>@aggTrade`. It is read-only and keyless, and nothing is ever sent on the socket.
  - `wss://data-stream.binance.vision` is added to the Ops Room `connect-src`.
  - Each partial book replaces the top 20 levels of the last REST book. Deeper levels keep their REST values. It updates the mid and `priceAt`.
  - Each aggregate trade goes into the same 300-trade tape the Hawkes and VPIN fit use.
  - The canyon repaints at most once a second.
- **Fallback**
  - REST polling keeps running. The desk, the court, the walls list and the breaker never depend on the socket.
  - On close the stream reconnects with backoff, from 1 s doubling to 60 s.
  - It pauses in a hidden tab unless the auto engine is on or a paper position is open.
  - The sonar tag shows the mode: `WS 100 ms`, `WS CONNECTING…`, `REST 5 s · WS RETRYING`, `REST 5 s · WS PAUSED` or `REST 5 s`.
- **Offline**
  - If no Binance book has arrived 15 s after load, the canyon draws a fixed, deterministic book in made-up units around 100.00.
  - It is labelled `SIMULATION · not market data` on the canvas and in the summary line.
  - It never enters `D.depth`, so the court, the auto engine, receipts, rings and every number elsewhere ignore it.
  - Once a real book has arrived it is never shown again in that session.

Date: 2026-10-23 · Status: Proposed (Ahmad's request of 2026-10-23 11:52Z: redesign and correct the whole site professionally, run a trial, review the plan with a team and pick the best fixes; merge waits for his go)
After Phase 15 (ADR-112) went live, all 23 snapshot sources answered in Pages run 39948702492. Two problems showed up in that live data:
- CIRCL pressure sat at 100, because 15 of the latest 30 records were critical.
- The Suez sea point returned no wave height.
A trial then ran the four pages (NABD Arabic and English, the Ops Room, THE CHAIN) at three sizes in light and dark. All 24 runs passed the overflow and console gate. Four read-only reviewers then looked at:
- design: screenshots plus Playwright measurements
- code correctness: reproductions with node and Playwright
- security: probes against a running proxy and a fake Ollama
- data honesty and copy: file and line checks
They reported 40 findings. This ADR records what was fixed and what was left, with reasons.
### Security (proxy `scripts/omega-data-proxy.mjs`)
- **DNS rebinding.** Every request whose `Host` is not a known name is refused with 421. Known names are `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `[::1]`; under `--lan` this machine's interface addresses and `*.ts.net` (Tailscale Serve); plus anything listed in `OMEGA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
  - Before: `Host: rebind.attacker.test:8796` with a matching Origin got 200 and the model list.
  - After: 421.
- **Local model reachable from any website.** A sandboxed iframe sends `Origin: null`, and a `text/plain` POST needs no preflight.
  - `/llm/*` now refuses `Origin: null` and any non-loopback origin (403).
  - It requires `Content-Type: application/json` (415).
- **Local model limits.**
  - One generation at a time; the rest get 429.
  - A request body that stalls for 10 s gets 408. Before, the socket was held until Node's 300 s limit.
  - The Ollama call is aborted when the page closes the connection.

Phase 18 arrived as one pasted conversation with another assistant, ending with Ahmad's ask: develop these for the site, research free and reliable open sources, upgrade the site, design the agent ("the super agent") and the whole site without errors, and do the maximum upgrade.
The conversation covered:

2. Building a simulation-only trading platform. That meant market data, a paper trading engine, technical indicators (RSI, MACD, moving averages) and a system that learns. It said a real platform needs a licence; in Kuwait that is the Capital Markets Authority.

docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-07 · Status: Proposed. Ahmad's message of 2026-11-07 asked:
- that a text and background pair that misses DESIGN.md's floor (WCAG ≥ 4.5:1, 3:1 for large text, and APCA |Lc| ≥ 60) be healed rather than only refused;
- for a deterministic bisection of at most 16 steps on the lightness L of `oklch(L C H)`, keeping C and H, to the nearest L that passes both, on dark and light backgrounds alike;
- for it in the server and the skill, in the reversal engine (with the colour, WCAG and APCA Lc before and after in the reversal log), and as an "Auto-Heal Contrast" button and report in the Studio.
1. **`jarvis/server/lib/contrast-heal.mjs`** (pure; inlined into the page).
   - **Colours:** `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `oklch(L C H)`.
   - **Conversion:** sRGB ↔ OKLab ↔ OKLCH with Björn Ottosson's matrices.
   - **Formulas:** WCAG 2's ratio, and APCA-W3 0.1.9's Lc (the constants the repository's contrast gate and the Studio badge use).
   - **`healOklchContrast(fg, bg, { large, minLc })`:**
     - It tries both ends (L = 1 and L = 0), and bisects 16 times between the current L and each end that passes.
     - It keeps the passing L nearest the original, which is lighter on a dark background and darker on a light one. Where both pass (large text, lower Lc), the nearer one wins.
     - Each candidate is judged on the 8-bit hex it would be written as, so the returned colour really passes.
   - **Gamut:** a lightness that leaves sRGB keeps its hue; chroma is lowered by bisection only as far as sRGB needs, and the result says `chromaReduced`. The first draft clipped channels, which moved a blue's hue by 12°; the server test caught it.
   - **No answer:** a pair that no lightness can fix (for example grey on the same grey, or blue on purple) comes back `ok: false` with the reason, and nothing is changed.

docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-14 · Status: Proposed. Ahmad's page of 2026-11-14 asked for the three ideas offered after ADR-162: Kahn's order for the skills in the composer, Sequence and Fallback nodes for the workbench stages, and UCT to choose a plan. The search half of that page (BM25 with RRF) is ADR-164.
1. **One engine, three rules.** `jarvis/server/lib/plan-order.mjs` is pure. It is inlined into the page in its own scope, and `.claude/skills/replica-plan-order/plan_order.py` gives the same answers (`tests/golden.json`, 97 requests).
2. **Kahn's order.** `kahnOrder(nodes, edges)` places, layer by layer, every node whose dependencies are placed, sorted by name, so one input always gives one order.
   - A node left over sits on a cycle or behind one. It is listed in `cycle` and left out of `order`; no edge is dropped to make the graph fit.
   - `orderKept` checks on its own that every edge between two placed nodes runs forwards. `verified` is that check.
3. **Skill dependencies are read, not guessed.** `plan_order.py deps` reads each skill's own Python files and records the other skills named in its `sys.path` statements (EXTRACTED). It writes `jarvis/app/data/skill-deps.json`: 59 skills, 21 links today.
   - `skillOrder` adds everything the chosen skills load and orders the lot.
   - The server reads the snapshot from disk. A `deps` field in the request is ignored.
4. **Behaviour tree.** `tickTree` ticks Sequence and Fallback nodes over leaves that are `success`, `failure` or `running`.
   - Sequence stops at the first child that is not success; Fallback stops at the first that is not failure. A leaf with no value is failure.
   - At most 8 levels, 100 nodes and 20 children a node.
5. **The workbench as a tree.** `workbenchTree` runs the ADR-160 workbench, then reads it as one Sequence:
   - the shield, the meta-codes and the request as leaves;
   - design, maths, atlas and security as Fallbacks of "ran" or "skipped";
   - the approvals last.
   A refused stage fails the tree

docs.title: ADR-164: Project search (BM25 and reciprocal rank fusion)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-14 · Status: Proposed. Ahmad's page of 2026-11-14 asked for the honest hybrid search offered after ADR-162 in place of the "quantum Grover search": BM25 with reciprocal rank fusion over the project's documents. ADR-163 covers the other half of that page.
1. **What is searched.** `.claude/skills/replica-project-search/project_search.py corpus` reads every ADR in `docs/adr`, every review in `docs/security` and every `SKILL.md` in `.claude/skills`, and writes `jarvis/app/data/search-corpus.json`. Each document keeps:
   - its title (the first `#` line, or a skill's `name`);
   - its first 20 `##` headings;
   - the first 2000 characters of the rest (a skill's `description` first).
2. **Three lexical rankers.** `jarvis/server/lib/project-search.mjs` is pure and is inlined into the page in its own scope. It uses the memory bank's tokenizer (ADR-138), which folds Arabic letter forms and drops stop words in both languages.
   - **body:** Okapi BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75) over the title, headings and text;
   - **field:** the same BM25 over the title and headings only;
   - **title:** character trigrams of the query against each title, kept at a Dice score of 0.3 or more, so a misspelt name still matches.
3. **Fusion.** RRF(d) = the sum over the three lists of 1 / (k + rank), with k = 60 and each list cut at 50. Ties go by id, so one query always gives one order. Each result shows its rank and score in every list that found it.
4. **Honesty.** Nothing is semantic, learned or guessed.
   - A document that shares no word or title trigram with the query is not found, and the page says «Nothing found».
   - An Arabic query finds Arabic text; it does not translate.
   - The snippet is a line of the document as written.
   - This replaces the "quantum Grover" label: ranking scores on a normal computer is not a quantum search.
5. **The same answers in Python:** `project_search.py` (`tests/golden.json`: 39 queries and 15 corpora, refusals included).
6. **Server:** `POST /ap

- requests the server sends on its own (outgoing webhooks, scheduled runs);
- a long-lived stream (server-sent events).

**What is not added:**

- Each hook's secret is the HMAC-SHA256 of its id under a 32-byte master key. The key sits in `jarvis/server/.data/webhook-master.key` (mode 0600), and `.data/` is gitignored.
- No secret is stored in the database, git or the browser.

Date: 2026-11-05 · Reviewer: Claude Code, cloud sandbox.
Ahmad asked on 2026-11-05 for a local Ollama bridge in the Jarvis server, with its own security review. AGENTS.md §1 needs a written review before any new service is added.
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `jarvis/server/lib/ollama-bridge.mjs` | Network side: talks to Ollama on 127.0.0.1 |
| `jarvis/server/lib/llm-plan.mjs` | Pure rules: thinking split, plan parsing, locks, fallback plan |

- No dependency.
- Nothing under `.claude/skills/`.
- No model weights in git.

- another host, including `localhost`, `[::1]` and `127.0.0.1.nip.io`;
- `https`, `file`;
- credentials, a path, a query.
No request, header or model answer can change the address afterwards.
Every call uses:
- `redirect: "error"`;
- `AbortSignal.timeout` (1.5 s for status, 45 s for a generation);
- a 2 MB answer cap.

- nine refused addresses;
- a server that will not start with `http://169.254.169.254`;
- every request the fake Ollama received was addressed to `127.0.0.1:<port>`.

Model names must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,62}(:tag)?$`. `:cloud` and `-cloud` models are refused, bec

Use when adding, changing or reading the Ops Room system self-test (shield button or ?selftest=1), now 24 checks. Fixed fixtures plus live data, read-only probes, honest failures, and the release gate before a PR.
# The 24-check self-test and the release gate (ADR-107 to ADR-110)
The self-test runs in the browser from the shield button or with `?selftest=1`. It reads the page through the frozen, read-only `window.OMEGA_PROBE` hooks and runs pure functions on fixed input. It never moves paper money, issues a receipt, opens a trade or sends a request other than reading public data or a tile.
- Each entry in `CHECKS` is `[English name, Arabic name, async () => ({ ok, why })]`, with a 20 s limit per check.
- A check has two halves: a fixture half (fixed input, exact expected answer) and, where the feature depends on data, a live half. When the live data is missing the check fails and `why` says which source and its state, with "تعذر التحقق منها". Never pass a check on a fixture alone when its name promises live data, and never relax a threshold to get green.
- `why` lists the measured numbers (counts, ratios, µs, tiers), so a reader can see why it passed.
- Motion is frozen during the run (`omega:selftest-start`); a check may assert that nothing animates.
- Update the count in the shield button's `aria-label`, the header comment and DESIGN.md §5 when the list changes.

# Research tools through the awesome lists
Curated awesome lists are a better first filter than star counts: every entry was reviewed by a
maintainer. Use them to build the candidate list, then verify each candidate yourself.
- Index of indexes: https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome (raw: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sindresorhus/awesome/main/readme.md)

This skill should be used when the user wants to "package an MCP server", "bundle an MCP", "make an MCPB", "ship a local MCP server", "distribute a local MCP", discusses ".mcpb files", mentions bundling a Node or Python runtime with their MCP server, or needs an MCP server that interacts with the local filesystem, desktop apps, or OS and must be installable without the user having Node/Python set up.
# Build an MCPB (Bundled Local MCP Server)
MCPB is a local MCP server **packaged with its runtime**. The user installs one file; it runs without needing Node, Python, or any toolchain on their machine. It's the sanctioned way to distribute local MCP servers.
> MCPB is the **secondary** distribution path. Anthropic recommends remote MCP servers for directory listing — see https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/what-to-build.
**Use MCPB when the server must run on the user's machine** — reading local files, driving a desktop app, talking to localhost services, OS-level APIs. If your server only hits cloud APIs, you almost certainly want a remote HTTP server instead (see `build-mcp-server`). Don't pay the MCPB packaging tax for something that could be a URL.
---
```
my-server.mcpb              (zip archive)
├── manifest.json           ← identity, entry point, config schema, compatibility
├── server/                 ← your MCP server code
│   ├── index.js
│   └── node_modules/       ← bundled dependencies (or vendored)
└── icon.png
```
The host reads `manifest.json`, launches `server.mcp_config.command` as a **stdio** MCP server, and pipes messages. From your code's perspective it's identical to a local stdio server — the only difference is packaging.

docs.text:
Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
# Frontend Design
Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.
If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.
Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.
Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the defau

Best practices for doing quick exploratory data analysis with minimal code and a Pandas .plot like API using HoloViews hvPlot.
# hvPlot Development Skills
This document provides best practices for developing plots and charts with HoloViz hvPlot in notebooks and .py files.
Please develop as an **Expert Python Developer** developing advanced data-driven, analytics and testable data visualisations, dashboards and applications would do. Keep the code short, concise, documented, testable and professional.
Core dependencies provided with the `hvplot` Python package:
- **hvplot**: Core visualization framework
- **holoviews**: Declarative data visualization library with composable elements. Best for: complex multi-layered plots, advanced interactivity (linked brushing, selection), when you need fine control over plot composition, scientific visualizations. More powerful but steeper learning curve than hvPlot. hvPlot is built upon holoviews.
- **colorcet**: Perceptually uniform colormaps
- **panel**: Provides widgets and layouts enabling tool, dashboard and data app development.
- **param**: A declarative approach to creating classes with typed, validated, and documented parameters. Fundamental to the reactive programming model of hvPlot and the rest of the HoloViz ecosystem.
- **pandas**: Industry-standard DataFrame library for tabular data. Best for: data cleaning, transformation, time series analysis, datasets that fit in memory. The default choice for most data work.
Optional dependencies from the HoloViz Ecosystem:
- **datashader**: Renders large datasets (millions+ points) into images for visualization. Best for: big data visualization, geospatial datasets, scatter plots with millions of points, heatmaps of dense data. Requires hvPlot or HoloViews as frontend.
- **geoviews**: Geographic data visualization with map projections and tile sources. Best for: geographic/geospatial plots, map-based dashboards, when you need coordinate systems and projections. Built on HoloVie

Use when changing the continuous-time (liquid) dynamics of the Ops Room neural flow 139 → 48 → 36 → 48 → 24 → 16 → 8, its τ table, shock events, Heun solver, settle animation or the oscilloscope's τ readout. The resting state must equal the trained feed-forward answer.
# Continuous-time neural flow (ADR-110)
The deep neural flow (`neural-flow-decision-viz`, ADR-109) is trained as an ordinary feed-forward network. ADR-110 lets it run in continuous time between readings, so the drawing shows a change travelling from the inputs to the heads. Training, targets and the decision rules do not change.
For neuron i of layer k:
  dx_i/dt = (σ(Σ_j W_ij x_j(t) + b_i) − x_i(t)) / τ_i(t)
- σ is ReLU in hidden layers and tanh in the 8 heads. Layer k is driven by layer k−1 as it is now, not as it will settle, so depth adds delay.
- This normalised leaky form has the feed-forward answer as its only resting state for any τ. Do not switch to the unnormalised `−x/τ + σ(·)` form: its rest is τ·σ(·), which would make the heads disagree with the trained network.
- τ_i = τ_layer · spread_i / (1 + κ·E), floored at τ_layer · spread_i / 8. τ_layer = [0.6, 0.9, 1.2, 1.6, 2.0, 2.5] s, κ = 4, spread_i a fixed 0.7 to 1.3 per neuron.
- E = Σ w · exp(−age / 30 s) over shock events. Shocks come only from `omega:shock` (whale wall, InfoCON rise, emergency squawk, BGP origin or more-specific change) and a microprice move of 0.5 bps or more.
- Explicit Heun (predictor-corrector, second order) in `nn.odeStep`, sub-steps h ≤ τ_min / 2, at most 4000 per call. The leak term is stable for h/τ ≤ 2, so the bound has margin.
- `nn.odeInit(net, x)` starts at rest; `nn.odeGap(net, x, st)` is the largest distance to rest.
- The page advances the state before each reading (dt capped at 120 s) and, after a new reading, runs a settle loop on `requestAnimationFrame` that stops when the gap is below 1e-3 or after 6 s. No loop runs at rest, under `prefers-reduced-motion`, or while the self-test runs.

# MCP Server Development Guide
Create MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. The quality of an MCP server is measured by how well it enables LLMs to accomplish real-world tasks.
---
# Process
Creating a high-quality MCP server involves four main phases:
### Phase 1: Deep Research and Planning
#### 1.1 Understand Modern MCP Design
**API Coverage vs. Workflow Tools:**
Balance comprehensive API endpoint coverage with specialized workflow tools. Workflow tools can be more convenient for specific tasks, while comprehensive coverage gives agents flexibility to compose operations. Performance varies by client—some clients benefit from code execution that combines basic tools, while others work better with higher-level workflows. When uncertain, prioritize comprehensive API coverage.
**Tool Naming and Discoverability:**
Clear, descriptive tool names help agents find the right tools quickly. Use consistent prefixes (e.g., `github_create_issue`, `github_list_repos`) and action-oriented naming.
**Context Management:**
Agents benefit from concise tool descriptions and the ability to filter/paginate results. Design tools that return focused, relevant data. Some clients support code execution which can help agents filter and process data efficiently.
**Actionable Error Messages:**
Error messages should guide agents toward solutions with specific suggestions and next steps.

4. **Write** (`report`, `markdown`): verbatim abstract sentences picked by maximal marginal relevance, each with its `[n]`; a counter-evidence section; a gaps list; numbered references with grade, indexes, open full text and Wayback capture.

docs.title: param
docs.text:
Use when building Python classes with validated, typed parameters using the Param library. Triggers include creating configuration classes, building reusable components with state, implementing reactive dependencies between parameters, adding type-safe attributes with bounds/constraints, creating testable parameterized classes, or when users mention param.Parameterized, @param.depends, or param.watch.
# Param: Declarative Parameters
Create typed, validated class attributes with reactive programming support.
```python
# DO always add this to ignore pyright Parameter type annotation warnings
# pyright: reportAssignmentType=false
import param
class Greeter(param.Parameterized):
    """A greeting generator with history tracking."""
    # DON'T use 'name' as parameter - it's reserved in Param
    # DO add type annotations, defaults, and doc strings
    target: str = param.String(default="World", doc="Name to greet")
    greeting: str = param.Selector(default="Hello", objects=["Hello", "Hi", "Hey"])
    count: int = param.Integer(default=1, bounds=(1, 10), doc="Repetitions")
    history: list = param.List(default=[], doc="Greeting history")
    # DO use @param.depends (watch=False) for computed values with no side effects
    @param.depends("target", "greeting", "count")
    def message(self) -> str:
        """Computed value - recalculates when dependencies change."""
        return " ".join([f"{self.greeting}, {self.target}!"] * self.count)
    # DO use @param.depends(watch=True) for side effects (state updates, I/O, etc.)
    @param.depends("target", watch=True)
    def _track_changes(self):
        """Side effect - automatically runs when target changes."""
        self.history = self.history + [self.target]
# Usage
greeter = Greeter(target="Alice")
print(greeter.message())      # "Hello, Alice!"
greeter.target = "Bob"
print(greeter.history)        # ["Bob"] - tracked the change
greeter.greeting = "Hi"
greeter.count = 2
print(greeter.message())      # "Hi, Bob! Hi, Bo

Two tools in this folder, both standard-library Python, no installs:

exact look is its trade dress, and it changes before launch.

what the original's users hate, in their own words, and fixes it in yours.

headings: The state machine of a plan
docs.text:
Proves properties of a plan or workflow by breadth-first search over its state machine - no deadlock, every step reachable, and no money, publish, permissions, install or outbound effect reachable without a locked approval (with a counterexample path when it is) - checks that UI components have default, hover, focus-visible, loading, empty, error and locked states, and lists the mutants of a Python module with a static test-strength estimate. Standard-library Python only; no network, no processes.
# replica-formal-verify
```bash
python3 .claude/skills/replica-formal-verify/state_prover.py --plan plan.json
python3 .claude/skills/replica-formal-verify/state_prover.py --machine machine.json --json
python3 .claude/skills/replica-formal-verify/state_prover.py --ui jarvis/app/src/app.css --components btn,input,select
python3 .claude/skills/replica-formal-verify/mutation_audit.py .claude/skills/replica-ux-physics/ux_physics.py --tests .claude/skills/replica-ux-physics/tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/replica-formal-verify/tests
```
`start`, one state per step, an effect state `e<i>` after each sensitive approval, and the terminals `done` and `stopped`. Steps follow their `depends`; a gate can fail to `stopped`; an approval can be rejected to `stopped`, and a sensitive one reaches its effect only on `approved`.
| Property | How it is proved |
| --- | --- |
| Deadlock freedom | every reachable state that is not a terminal has a way out |
| Reachability | every step is reached from `start`, and `done` is reachable |
| Safety (AGENTS.md §1) | remove the locked approval states and search again: no effect may be reached; if one is, the path to it is printed |
The search is exhaustive over a finite graph, so "verified" is a proof for the machine as built, not a test of a few runs. It says nothing about what a tool does inside a step.

docs.text:
A structural knowledge graph of Jarvis without a vector database - screens, API routes, server modules, SQL tables with their constraints, and skills with their Python tools, joined by what each one calls - read from the code with ast and plain text parsing, written as JSON for the Governance page's SVG map. Rebuild the page afterwards (`node jarvis/scripts/build-app.mjs`, then `skillspector-audit.mjs --fix`).
| Node | Read from |
| --- | --- |
| screen | `pages.<name>` in `jarvis/app/src/app.js`, nav routes in `shell.tmpl` |
| route | `jarvis/server/server.mjs`: `R("GET", /^…$/)`, `rest === "/…"`, `(k = /^…$/.exec(rest))` blocks |

- route → module (the object the route awaits);
- module → table (SQL in that file);

docs.text:
Run long, multi-step tasks without losing the thread - three plan files on disk, SHA-256 chained state capsules to resume after /clear, and an evidence gate that blocks "done" until tests pass.
# replica-long-horizon
Long tasks fail in three ways: the plan drifts out of the context window, work is lost when the
session is cleared, and steps get marked done before anything proved them. This skill fixes each
with one stdlib-only Python tool:
| Problem | Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context rot | `plan.py` | Keeps the plan, the findings and the progress log in three files on disk. Re-read them; never trust memory. |
| Lost work after `/clear` or a crash | `capsule.py` | Saves a SHA-256 hash-chained capsule of the three files, the git position and the changed files (optionally with their content). Verifies and restores. |
| "Done" without proof | `gate.py` | Marks a task done only when its evidence logs pass, are fresher than the code they cover, and its numbered acceptance criteria have recorded evidence. |
No tool starts a process, opens a socket or runs code it reads. The agent runs the real commands
(tests, `verify-contrast.mjs`, SkillSpector) and saves their output; the gate reads those files.
This keeps the skill at SkillSpector 0 critical, 0 high, and it means a gate result is only as
honest as the logs: always produce them by redirecting the real command, never by hand.
`$SKILL` is this folder. `$W` is the task's working folder (for example `work/<task-name>/`).
```bash
python3 $SKILL/plan.py init $W --goal "Ship the agent editor" \
  --criteria "Editing an agent saves and reloads" --criteria "Locked rows can never be switched on"
```
Writes `task_plan.md` (goal, numbered acceptance criteria AC1…, phases and tasks T1…),
`findings.md` (facts, decisions, evidence) and `progress.md` (an append-only log). Then fill the
phases by hand. A task line names the checks it needs and the criteria it proves:
```

docs.title: replica-project-search
docs.text:
Search the repository's own documents - every ADR, every security review and every skill's SKILL.md - with three lexical rankers fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion - Okapi BM25 over the title, headings and text, BM25 over the title and headings only, and character trigrams of the query against each title so a misspelt name still matches. Arabic and English with the memory bank's tokenizer. Nothing is semantic or learned; with nothing shared, nothing is found and the answer says so. Standard-library Python only; it reads the repository's Markdown files to build the corpus and fetches nothing.
# replica-project-search
```bash
python3 .claude/skills/replica-project-search/project_search.py corpus --root . --out jarvis/app/data/search-corpus.json
python3 .claude/skills/replica-project-search/project_search.py search jarvis/app/data/search-corpus.json "contrast healer oklch"
python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/replica-project-search/tests
```
- Three rankers, each a list cut at 50: BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75) over the title, headings and text; the same BM25 over the title and headings; trigram Dice of at least 0.3 between the query and the title.
- RRF(d) = the sum over the lists of 1 / (k + rank), k = 60. Ties go by id, so one query always gives one order.
- The corpus keeps each document's title, its first 20 `##` headings and the first 2000 characters of its text. A word past that is not searched; the page says so.
- The snippet is a line of the document, as written, that holds a query word.
- These are word and letter matches. No meaning, synonym or translation is guessed: an Arabic query finds Arabic text and an English query finds English text.
- Same answers as `jarvis/server/lib/project-search.mjs`: `tests/golden.json`.

docs.title: replica-timeseries-math
docs.text:
Time-series maths in the standard library - Welford running mean and variance, EWMA, online z-score anomalies, a VPIN-style flow imbalance and LTTB downsampling that keeps peaks and troughs - for telemetry, build times or any [t, v] series, as JSON or CSV. The same formulas as Jarvis's server engine. Standard-library Python only; no network, no processes.
# replica-timeseries-math
```bash
python3 .claude/skills/replica-timeseries-math/ts_math.py series.json --threshold 120
python3 .claude/skills/replica-timeseries-math/ts_math.py series.csv --json
python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/replica-timeseries-math/tests
```
| Formula | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| Welford (1962): n, mean, M2 per value; variance = M2 / (n − 1) | mean and standard deviation in O(1) memory, exact |
| EWMA: e = α·x + (1 − α)·e | a smoothed level that follows recent values |
| z = (x − mean) / sd against the values before x | anomalies (\|z\| > 3 after 30 values), so a spike cannot hide itself |
| VPIN-style imbalance: tick-rule up/down ticks in equal buckets, mean \|up − down\| / size | 0 balanced, 1 one-way; borrowed from Easley, López de Prado and O'Hara (2012), so it carries `[INFERENCE]` |
| LTTB (Steinarsson, 2013) | n points cut to a drawing size, keeping the first, the last and the largest triangles, so peaks and troughs survive |
`jarvis/server/lib/timeseries.mjs` runs the same formulas inside the Jarvis server (no child process) and in the page. Keep the two in step; the tests check both against the same numbers.
- The z-score assumes a roughly steady series. For Gaussian noise, about 0.27 % of ordinary values pass |z| > 3; that is the rule working, not a bug.
- VPIN here measures direction changes in any metric. It is not the market measure and predicts nothing.

# Locked base, sweeps and the receipt ratchet
Paper only. The S key and "Sweep profit now" move paper money inside the paper ledger (ADR-093). A sweep of real funds stays a proposal in the Director 00 approval inbox.
- A first visit locks a $20.00 paper base with a LOCK receipt.
- Sweepable profit is `max(0, NetEquity − LockedBase)`, rounded to 1e-6 USDT. Swept profit moves to the paper safe and never back into trading.
- Next to every input say: the base itself can still lose in trading; only swept profit is protected. The circuit breaker is fixed rules, not a prediction.
`{invoice, seq, ts, mode, symbol, type, amount, before, after, reason, prev_hash, hash}` plus optional `exec` and `brain2`.

- Past 1000 receipts the oldest 500 fold into an `omega-merkle-checkpoint-v1` (parent = SHA-256 of left hex + right hex, an odd leaf pairs with itself). Checkpoints chain by `prev_checkpoint`.

# Software and interface architecture for OMEGA
Text rules only. `DESIGN.md` and `AGENTS.md` win where they say more. Distilled from this repository's own pages (ADR-087 to ADR-109).
- Space on the 4 / 8 scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48). Radii are concentric: outer = inner + padding (card 28 = 8 + 20).
- Colour is OKLCH tokens with a Display P3 variant under `@media (color-gamut: p3)`. One accent. Status colours mean status. Vivid `--apple-*` values are for strokes, fills and canvas marks, never text.
- Glass is `blur(32px) saturate(190%)` over `--glass` at 0.82 alpha, always with an opaque fallback outside `@supports`, and only on fixed or sticky chrome, map overlays, the Brain 2 causal card, the neural oscilloscope and X-Ray badges. Hairlines are 0.5 px with a specular top line.
- Zero clipped or overlapping text at 390×844 @3x, 1440×900 and 2560×1080, light and dark. Wrap long values with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; numbers stay tabular, `direction: ltr`, `unicode-bidi: isolate`. Nothing below 12 px, also on canvas.
- Motion uses `transform` and `opacity`, `--ease-apple-fluid`, and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Canvases animate only on events.
- Heavy maths runs in a Blob Web Worker on `Float64Array` buffers and posts results back; transfer buffers when the page does not need them again.
- Canvases size to `devicePixelRatio` (cap 3), draw on demand, batch strokes into `Path2D` groups, cache static layers offscreen, and pause under `IntersectionObserver` and `visibilitychange`.
- Telemetry is a bounded ring of 300. No `setInterval` faster than 1 s for rendering; requestAnimationFrame only while something moves.

docs.title: synaptic-spiderweb-viz
docs.text:
Use when changing the Brain 2 synaptic web canvas in the Ops Room - its rings of nodes, edges, pulses, glass causal card, gym panel or labels. Event-driven drawing, real readings only, accessible fallbacks.
# Brain 2 synaptic web
The web (`#brain2`, ADR-108) shows how the desk's inputs feed its decisions. It is a picture of real readings, not decoration.
- Outer ring, 10 sensory nodes: BGP/IODA, Cables, Orbits/Kp, Straits, Quakes (USGS), Weather (Open-Meteo), Aviation, GDELT, Mempool, SEC.
- Middle ring, 8 quant nodes: Microprice, Hawkes λ, VPIN, Kalman, BOCPD, Kyle λ/Ice, GEX/DVOL, Funding.
- Inner ring, 6 agents: Bull, Bear, Judge, Researcher, Modeler, Auditor.
- Core: Vault (the $20 locked base and the SHA-256 receipt chain).
- Edges are only the links the desk really uses. A node is filled when its source is live and hollow when offline; its arc is a 0–1 reading from the page's own numbers.
1. Draw on demand. A pulse fires only on a discrete event: microprice move of 0.5 bps or more, a new whale wall or iceberg, a new data pull, a gym burst, or the person's hover or tap. Never a loop.
2. At most one pulse per second. Under reduced motion there is no travelling light; the affected nodes are highlighted instead.
3. Pause under `IntersectionObserver` and `visibilitychange`. devicePixelRatio up to 3.
4. Labels are 12px minimum, placed after all nodes, at the first free spot (own side, mirror side, then one to three lines up or down). On a phone the web is an upright ellipse and labels sit above or below their nodes. Check 390×844 @3x screenshots for overlap.
5. Colours: `--apple-*` for strokes and fills, gated tokens for text.
Hover, tap or click opens the glass card for the nearest node, and the arrow keys step through the nodes when the canvas has focus: what it reads, its value with source and time, what it feeds, and `[INFERENCE]` where a heuristic is involved. Esc closes it. The "All 25 nodes" `<details>` list carries the same content as text for screen readers

Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.
# Theme Factory Skill
This skill provides a curated collection of professional font and color themes themes, each with carefully selected color palettes and font pairings. Once a theme is chosen, it can be applied to any artifact.
To apply consistent, professional styling to presentation slide decks, use this skill. Each theme includes:
- A cohesive color palette with hex codes
- Complementary font pairings for headers and body text
- A distinct visual identity suitable for different contexts and audiences
To apply styling to a slide deck or other artifact:
1. **Show the theme showcase**: Display the `theme-showcase.pdf` file to allow users to see all available themes visually. Do not make any modifications to it; simply show the file for viewing.
2. **Ask for their choice**: Ask which theme to apply to the deck
3. **Wait for selection**: Get explicit confirmation about the chosen theme
4. **Apply the theme**: Once a theme has been chosen, apply the selected theme's colors and fonts to the deck/artifact
The following 10 themes are available, each showcased in `theme-showcase.pdf`:
1. **Ocean Depths** - Professional and calming maritime theme
2. **Sunset Boulevard** - Warm and vibrant sunset colors
3. **Forest Canopy** - Natural and grounded earth tones
4. **Modern Minimalist** - Clean and contemporary grayscale
5. **Golden Hour** - Rich and warm autumnal palette
6. **Arctic Frost** - Cool and crisp winter-inspired theme
7. **Desert Rose** - Soft and sophisticated dusty tones
8. **Tech Innovation** - Bold and modern tech aesthetic
9. **Botanical Garden** - Fresh and organic garden colors
10. **Midnight Galaxy** - Dramatic and cosmic deep tones

docs.title: web-artifacts-builder
docs.text:
Suite of tools for creating elaborate, multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts using modern frontend web technologies (React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui). Use for complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components - not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts.
# Web Artifacts Builder
To build powerful frontend claude.ai artifacts, follow these steps:
1. Initialize the frontend repo using `scripts/init-artifact.sh`
2. Develop your artifact by editing the generated code
3. Bundle all code into a single HTML file using `scripts/bundle-artifact.sh`
4. Display artifact to user
5. (Optional) Test the artifact
**Stack**: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Parcel (bundling) + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui
VERY IMPORTANT: To avoid what is often referred to as "AI slop", avoid using excessive centered layouts, purple gradients, uniform rounded corners, and Inter font.
### Step 1: Initialize Project
Run the initialization script to create a new React project:
```bash
bash scripts/init-artifact.sh <project-name>
cd <project-name>
```
This creates a fully configured project with:
- ✅ React + TypeScript (via Vite)
- ✅ Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 with shadcn/ui theming system
- ✅ Path aliases (`@/`) configured
- ✅ 40+ shadcn/ui components pre-installed
- ✅ All Radix UI dependencies included
- ✅ Parcel configured for bundling (via .parcelrc)
- ✅ Node 18+ compatibility (auto-detects and pins Vite version)
### Step 2: Develop Your Artifact
To build the artifact, edit the generated files. See **Common Development Tasks** below for guidance.
### Step 3: Bundle to Single HTML File
To bundle the React app into a single HTML artifact:
```bash
bash scripts/bundle-artifact.sh
```
This creates `bundle.html` - a self-contained artifact with all JavaScript, CSS, and dependencies inlined. This file can be directly shared in Claude conversations as an artifact.
**Requirements**: Your project must have an `index.html` in the root directory.
**What the script does**:
- Installs bundling

docs.title: webapp-testing
docs.text:
Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.
# Web Application Testing
To test local web applications, write native Python Playwright scripts.
**Helper Scripts Available**:
- `scripts/with_server.py` - Manages server lifecycle (supports multiple servers)
**Always run scripts with `--help` first** to see usage. DO NOT read the source until you try running the script first and find that a customized solution is abslutely necessary. These scripts can be very large and thus pollute your context window. They exist to be called directly as black-box scripts rather than ingested into your context window.
```
User task → Is it static HTML?
    ├─ Yes → Read HTML file directly to identify selectors
    │         ├─ Success → Write Playwright script using selectors
    │         └─ Fails/Incomplete → Treat as dynamic (below)
    │
    └─ No (dynamic webapp) → Is the server already running?
        ├─ No → Run: python scripts/with_server.py --help
        │        Then use the helper + write simplified Playwright script
        │
        └─ Yes → Reconnaissance-then-action:
            1. Navigate and wait for networkidle
            2. Take screenshot or inspect DOM
            3. Identify selectors from rendered state
            4. Execute actions with discovered selectors
```
To start a server, run `--help` first, then use the helper:
**Single server:**
```bash
python scripts/with_server.py --server "npm run dev" --port 5173 -- python your_automation.py
```
**Multiple servers (e.g., backend + frontend):**
```bash
python scripts/with_server.py \
  --server "cd backend && python server.py" --port 3000 \
  --server "cd frontend && npm run dev" --port 5173 \
  -- python your_automation.py
```
